items: The toolbar marks the page or account on screen with the same background as hover, without a border; clicking an account button no longer leaves a focus outline.
The update button moved to the footer, next to the version (Windows).
Notification tests use a private test notification service, so they no longer crash when no notification daemon is running.
If file drop cannot be set up for a page, Whazapp logs it instead of stopping (Linux).
All GTK tests, including notifications, run together in a single test process.
A floating blur button on the chat page hides Messages, the Chat list, Images and media, or the Full screen; the choice is saved per account (Linux).
Check for updates verifies the installer against the release's SHA256SUMS and saves it to your Downloads folder.
Whazapp checks for updates by itself at most once every 24 hours.
Update checks read releases from github.com/azislamayuda/zWhazapp.
Documents opened from WhatsApp, such as PDFs, show in their own window when WebKit can display them; other file types go to the normal download flow (Linux).
An account whose page crashes reloads by itself, at most once a minute, instead of staying blank until you press Reload (Linux).
GTK tests share one GTK thread, so they run together in a single cargo test process.
Unread badges: each Whaz account button shows its unread chat count, and the total appears in the window title; the tray stays icon-only (Linux).
Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+1/2/3 open Whaz 1–3, Ctrl+, opens Settings, Ctrl+R or F5 reloads, Ctrl+Q quits (Linux). They are listed in Settings > General.
Settings > Accounts shows which accounts have camera or microphone permission and lets you forget it, so the next call asks again (Linux).
Settings > Accounts and the account switcher in the toolbar use the new WhatsApp chat icon.
Check for updates moved from the top toolbar to the footer, just before the version.
Settings no longer shows a Back to chats button; the footer text lines up with the Whazapp header.
Each Whaz account may now store up to 10% of the disk instead of WebKit's fixed 1000 MiB, the likely cause of WhatsApp's "not enough space" warning and the logout after it (Linux).
The chat lock accepts any password you choose; there is no minimum length or other rule.
Per-account memory limits now actually apply (WebKit rejected them before because of their order).
Smaller, cleaner stylesheet and icon set with identical layout.
Updated Rust dependencies to their latest compatible patch releases (Tauri 2.12.5, Wry 0.57.1).
Linux release tooling builds only the WebRTC AppImage; the DEB/RPM and system-WebKit AppImage scripts were removed.
One GitHub workflow builds, in order: validation, the Linux AppImage, the Windows EXE, the version tag and a draft release whose description lists only the new features and changes.
Removed unused code, icons and test helpers; tests follow the new app identity.

changes.category: Voice and video calls on Linux
items: Voice and video calls work in the Linux AppImage, which now ships its own WebKitGTK 2.55 runtime with WebRTC.
WhatsApp no longer reports "Your browser doesn't support calling": Whazapp provides the SharedArrayBuffer it requires.
Outgoing video no longer freezes and your own preview no longer spins: video calls use VP8/VP9 instead of the runtime's failing H.264 encoder.
"Switch to other window" opens a separate call window instead of asking to allow pop-ups; it closes when the call ends.
Allowing the camera and microphone once is remembered per account, also after restarting Whazapp.
Fixed a crash on the first video call and a prompt bug that denied the camera after the microphone prompt.
The screen no longer sleeps or locks during a call, and can sleep again when the call ends.
Settings > Check calling capabilities names exactly what WhatsApp is missing and tests the video encoders.
Linux releases are AppImage only; DEB and RPM are discontinued because distribution WebKitGTK packages cannot make calls. Windows stays an .exe installer.
New application identity io.azislamayuda.whazapp.desktop. Profiles and settings of earlier versions stay in the old io.whazapp.desktop folders; link WhatsApp again or copy them manually.
Account pages run in WebKit's sandbox, with hardware-accelerated video rendering in the AppImage.
Lower memory use per account: no in-memory resource cache or back/forward cache, and each account's web process frees memory earlier without ever being closed for it.
Code cleanup: one WhatsApp origin check, one chat-lock check per account switch, and no lint warnings in app or tests.
Moved top navigation icons to the right and added a small Whazapp tagline.
Moved the installed version and GitHub author to a bottom-right footer.
Added an on-demand GitHub release check with toast feedback; updates are downloaded manually.
Preserved existing account profiles and login storage.
Soft green desktop interface with responsive navigation, English UI, and Light, Dark, and System themes.
Rust and Tauri desktop application for Linux, with Windows 10/11 x64 source and installer tooling.
Official WhatsApp Web QR linking in the main window, persistent local sessions, and three isolated Whaz account slots.
Single-instance activation, system tray controls, optional hidden tray icon, and background startup after desktop sign-in.
Desktop notifications with click-to-open, Do Not Disturb, sound preferences, and hidden message previews.
Settings with About, changelog, notification testing, and browser calling capability diagnostics.
Privacy blur for the entire page or selected areas, plus password-protected chat access and Lock now.
Encrypted backup and restore for settings and manually imported contact/chat archives; live WhatsApp databases and login sessions are excluded.
File downloads, multi-file drag and drop, image/sticker attachment modes, and clipboard compatibility improvements.
Linux AppImage, DEB, and RPM build tooling, plus a Windows NSIS installer workflow.
Remote WhatsApp views are separated from trusted local Tauri commands; external navigation requires a user action.
Camera and microphone use requires permission. Linux voice/video calling depends on WebKit capabilities and is not a verified feature of this release.
This initial public version consolidates pre-repository development. Experimental WebRTC runtimes are not included.
